about: Canada answer key rule changes and what each one touches (Brandon t915u, Nov 9 2026 4:40 PM CST; KZ4CP 5:12 PM CST). Part of the Canada rules hash. Same format as .github/us-key-rule-scope.json (states = ['CA-ON', ...]). The Canada builder reads the whole country in one job, so any declared province rebuilds the whole Canada key; a change that touches no province rebuilds nothing. Nov 9 evening (KZ4CP 5:41 PM CST): a scope may also list park refs, 'parks': ['US-1234', ...]: only those parks are re-matched (their states are read again, every other park there keeps its result). A scope that lists nothing means ALL; a change that touches no park says scope 'none'.

changes.why: Bad-ID block list (Brandon t919u); the list is empty, so no current result changes.

Every services*.arcgis.com host (services2 to services9 too) is saved-copy only on every path, the GeoJSON and zipped-shapefile pulls included. The Parks Canada layer on one of those hosts covers every province and territory, so the scope is all.

services-<region>.arcgis.com hosts (services-eu1 and the like) count as services*.arcgis.com (saved copy only, robots.txt included), and ncnhde.natureserve.org is never contacted. The Parks Canada layer is on one of those hosts and covers every province and territory, so the scope is all.

The Canada key takes a CHECKED hand file (KPC_CA_HAND, hand-CA.<name>.geojson.gz on the boundary-cache release) for a layer a bot may not read, e.g. Parks Canada's own places layer on a saved-copy-only host: fail closed on a short file, keep-bigger against the saved records of that layer, then the saved copy is saved again. No join rule changes; Parks Canada places cover every province and territory, so the scope is all.

Review fixes to the readers. CPCAD and every provincial layer are read whole or not at all (count and ids checked; a stalled or ignored page offset is an error); a source that fails takes its records from the saved copy and nothing is saved in a run where a source failed. robots.txt is asked for the first address and every redirect hop, as the US key does. Host rules come from the one shared guard. One Canada-wide file, so the scope is all.

Official pin fills (kpc_pin_fill.py; KPC-Data data/intake/official-pins-nov12.json, the pin-fill rows marked ready): a park POTA has no usable pin for (absent or 0,0) is joined by its official pin and marked pf; a POTA pin is never moved and a fill is ignored once POTA has a usable pin. The 22 ready Canada fills are all Quebec parks (CA-1974 CA-1997 CA-2056 CA-2058 CA-2064 CA-2080 CA-2082 CA-2089 CA-2092 CA-2093 CA-2097 CA-2099 CA-2103 CA-2198 CA-2223 CA-2227 CA-2228 CA-2238 CA-2241 CA-2246 CA-2261 CA-2274), so only CA-QC results change; no other province has a ready fill.

Quality must-fix M2: kpc_pin_fill.py is in the Canada RULE_FILES (removed from NOT_RULES). A later edit to it moves the Canada hash. No join result changes (the builders already called it); no province is rebuilt for this alone.
